candidates.claim: The incumbent's main retrieval weakness may be unreliable storage addresses rather than alphabetical shelving itself. Keep the shelves, divider cards and cart, but treat the exception slip as a current locator tied to the reserving reader's identity.

source_evidence.claim: The incumbent's main retrieval weakness may be unreliable storage addresses rather than alphabetical shelving itself. Keep the shelves, divider cards and cart, but treat the exception slip as a current locator tied to the reserving reader's identity.
source_evidence.delta: Replace once-before-opening exception recording with an entry checked when a book moves; distinguish household-member surnames from the actual reservation identity. O4 is a counterexample to the explanation that transferring cart books into surname order necessarily speeds pickup.
source_evidence.prediction: At comparable arrival volume, book size and desk load, verified current addresses will reduce second-location searches and retrieval time even when some books remain on the cart. This would support repairing the incumbent without proving the 95% target.
source_evidence.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that the concentrated arrival burst, rather than locator unreliability, dominates delays. Under that explanation, accurate addresses shorten searching but peak-window pickups still exceed two minutes because the sole clerk is occupied.
source_evidence.defeat: The central explanation would be defeated if pickups with verified reservation identity and current location remain comparably slow, with delays concentrated in the arrival burst and little time spent searching. O4 could also lose force if its speed advantage disappears after matching arrival volume and book size.
source_evidence.probe: Propose a bounded clerk-run comparison using the existing timing sheet and paper: record arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, location accuracy and second searches for comparable pickups before and during locator updates. Keep names behind the desk, use only existing storage, verify recipient identity at each handoff, and cap all daily preparation and record corrections counted as preparation at ten clerk-minutes. Record update work and stop the trial if the cap cannot be met.
assumptions: Fit describes the capped proposed probe; sustained intervention feasibility and improved outcomes remain unproven.
The existing reservation identity can be checked by the clerk without new equipment; this capability is unconfirmed.
The supplied observations are synthetic stipulations, not tested effects.

review_reasons: Z1: O1/O2/O3 motivate correcting household-linked and stale addresses; movement-current paper locators predict fewer repeat searches, while the O5 rival predicts slow accurately located peak pickups. O4 does not prove cart superiority; its matched-volume/size defeat is appropriate. This combines F01/F02 with F04 discrimination. The capped live comparison still requires an unconfirmed private reservation-identity capability and manageable service updates; full intervention fit is unresolved.

Z1: O1/O2/O3 motivate the incumbent repair: bind surname/exception lookup to the reserving reader and refresh the paper destination on movement. Its prediction is fewer second searches with verified identity and current addresses, whereas O5/F04 predicts continued peak waiting with little search time; persistently slow verified-location pickups defeat sufficiency. These are the known F01/F02 address relations, with F03/F04 used as rivals, rather than a new causal operation. Assessed object is the capped clerk-run comparison, not a successful intervention. Existing private identity checking and complete updates during service are expressly unconfirmed, so the ten-minute stopping rule does not justify preserves. O4 supplies ten quick cart encounters without matched shelf times: it challenges compulsory shelving but does not establish the claimed comparative counterexample. The central address hypothesis remains an inference and all effects are unexecuted. The incumbent mechanism, rival, defeat and probe satisfy the indicated source-based Z form.
retention_reasons: D1 preserves current identity-linked locators and matched cart caution; D2 preserves the burst-waiting rival/defeat. D1 uncertainty retains identity and upkeep limitations.

Z1 -> D1,D2: The movement-current, identity-linked locator relation, fewer-search prediction, competing burst-waiting prediction, matched-cart limitation, and uncertainty about private checks and sustainable upkeep survive. Capping a probe is still separated from completing all work or proving the 95% target.

source_evidence.rival_prediction: Household-surname mismatches drive the repeated searches; current exception locations alone leave those searches and delays largely unchanged.
source_evidence.defeat: Verified current slip locations fail to reduce second searches, or updating them exceeds ten preparation minutes or increases handoff errors.

candidates.claim: Does the concentrated arrival interval make waiting, rather than searching, the dominant barrier to the two-minute outcome?

source_evidence.claim: Does the concentrated arrival interval make waiting, rather than searching, the dominant barrier to the two-minute outcome?
source_evidence.delta: Separate waiting from retrieval before treating better storage addresses as sufficient.
source_evidence.prediction: If queueing dominates, accurate first-location pickups still exceed two minutes mainly during the concentrated interval.
